protocol.py: 6 biology problems (3 errors, 1 warning, 2 notes).

1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 15 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at
least)
   line 52:  p300.aspirate(15, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 52 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 15 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul (this
   line did it 96 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong
   amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator
   passes the move. Wells: well A1 in slot 2.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [651065ba4d91]

2. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 2: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 52:  p300.aspirate(15, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 52 the p300_single_gen2 draws 15 ul from mix (well A1 in slot 2) with its tip 1
   mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 190 ul, which in this NEST 12
   Well Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.89 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air
   (this line did it twice, after 94 times in the liquid; 30 ul of air in all). The
   simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 2 wells filled from these
   draws got air instead of liquid.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 2.
   Also reached 2 other wells: wells H11 and H12 in slot 3.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 258 ul in it for the surface to
   reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube
   lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [35e6c7c7d67b]

3. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 5 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at least)
   line 58:  p300.aspirate(5, source_well)
   At line 58 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 5 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul (this
   line did it 96 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong
   amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator
   passes the move. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 88 more in slot 4.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 88 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [0640d8fc8230]

4. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 94 stocks
   line 58:  p300.aspirate(5, source_well)
   At line 58 the tip went into source_A1 (well A1 in slot 4), source_A2 (well A2 in slot
   4), source_A3 (well A3 in slot 4), source_A4 (well A4 in slot 4) and 90 more while it
   still carried mix (well A1 in slot 2) from an earlier step (this line did it 94 times). A
   tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so
   these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. The protocol does not draw
   from them again, so this run is not harmed, but what is left in the stock is no longer
   clean for the next run.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 86 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 58 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [a319c1e4bcd0]

5. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 94 wells of mix with a sample
   line 55:  p300.dispense(15, dest_well)
   At line 55 the robot starts putting mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3), and
   94 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the mix
   without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated, or
   the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate can
   tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 86 more in
   slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 86 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 15 ul of mix and 5 ul of water in place of the
   template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [febef65aa643]

6. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 94 wells never mixed after source_A1, source_A2, source_A3,
source_A4 and 90 more went in (25% of the well)
   line 61:  p300.dispense(5, dest_well)
   At line 61 the robot added source_A1, source_A2, source_A3, source_A4 and 90 more to
   wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 86 more in slot 3, which already held mix (this
   line did it 94 times). The addition was 25% of the well, nothing mixed the well
   afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do
   not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated.
   A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be,
   mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 86 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 86 more in slot 3 after line 61:
   `mix_after=(5, 16)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 16, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [6f9527df4eef]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.explanation: At line 58 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 5 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul (this line did it 96 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 88 more in slot 4.
findings.fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: 94 stocks
findings.explanation: At line 58 the tip went into source_A1 (well A1 in slot 4), source_A2 (well A2 in slot 4), source_A3 (well A3 in slot 4), source_A4 (well A4 in slot 4) and 90 more while it still carried mix (well A1 in slot 2) from an earlier step (this line did it 94 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. The protocol does not draw from them again, so this run is not harmed, but what is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 58 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: No no-template control: 94 wells of mix with a sample
findings.explanation: At line 55 the robot starts putting mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3), and 94 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 86 more in slot 3.
findings.fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 15 ul of mix and 5 ul of water in place of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.

findings.title: 94 wells never mixed after source_A1, source_A2, source_A3, source_A4 and 90 more went in (25% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 61 the robot added source_A1, source_A2, source_A3, source_A4 and 90 more to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 86 more in slot 3, which already held mix (this line did it 94 times). The addition was 25% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 86 more in slot 3 after line 61: `mix_after=(5, 16)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 16, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
